markdown_report:
The best first experiment remains a distance-resolved diagnostic adapter for the supplied NextItNet. At 0% progress, trustworthy measurements should precede architectural changes; the adapter’s value is troubleshooting, with validation improvement still unproven.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Existing margins measure sampled training separation, not the reported preference for specific recent matches. Positive score rescaling can enlarge margins without changing ranking, so margins need rank-based companions.
2. Left padding makes readout and deployment consistency essential. Selecting `count−1` can inspect padding or an earlier interaction; adapter correctness alone cannot establish generated-predictor correctness.
3. Available text supports lexical evidence, while histories support behavioral sensitivity. Neither establishes compatibility, satisfied needs, latent intent, or simulator traits; unavailable measurements require explicit support and missingness.

**Insights from related work**

1. NextItNet’s causal dilations determine reachable offsets [1,5]. Maximum receptive-field span alone does not establish that every intervening position is reachable; normalization across time can also invalidate causality.
2. Shuffling studies question assumptions about sequential structure [2,7]. Deletion additionally changes surviving items’ distances, so perturbation responses mix evidence dependence and convolutional geometry.
3. Sampled recommendation metrics can reverse model comparisons [3]. Stability and accuracy are also distinct outcomes [8]; preserve the pinned macro validation HR@10 and confirm repairs through controlled ablations.

**Framework and directions**

| Direction | Evidence | Gap addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation integrity | Reachable offsets, padding, causality, checkpoint parity | Incorrect readout, leakage, deployment mismatch |
| Temporal dependence | Prefix shuffle, matched recent/older ablations, fixed versus repacked positions | Unknown dependence and perturbation artifacts |
| Evidence quality | Supports, missing text, unavailable values, paired uncertainty | Unsupported behavioral interpretations |

**Candidate ideas and assessments**

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means more work.

- **Distance-resolved adapter — 4/6/5.** Originality: integrates architecture-aware controls, although its components are established. Potential: identifies actionable implementation failures, although sensitivity has no demonstrated link to repair gains. Difficulty: reuses hooks, although exact reachability, embedding ablation and predictor parity require model-specific work [1,2,5,6].
- **Recent-suffix auxiliary loss — 4/6/4.** Originality: applies familiar augmentation to the diagnosis, although incremental. Potential: may strengthen recent evidence, although it can suppress persistent preferences or teach a latest-item shortcut. Difficulty: shares one backbone and head, although another forward pass consumes budget [1,2].
- **Support-aware lexical audit — 3/5/3.** Originality: connects title evidence with ranking, although overlap is conventional. Potential: exposes vague matches, although it cannot verify practical fit. Difficulty: needs no pretrained weights, although identifier extraction requires safeguards [4].

**Selected algorithm**

Freeze each category’s actual model. Retain all-position margins separately; compare final-position scores under final-item-preserving prefix shuffles and matched recent/older removals. Pair deletion/repacking with slot-preserving embedding ablation of identical events; their difference measures implementation sensitivity, not a pure compression effect. Report fixed-candidate rank changes, top-10 overlap, raw margins and supports separately.

Verify exact reachable offsets, future-token invariance, aligned-prefix equivalence and saved-predictor score parity. Preserve padding, targets, model mode and local RNG state; mark unsupported values unavailable. Use repeated deterministic perturbations and user-level uncertainty only when IDs exist. Do not call loader-pair diagnostics HR@10. Any validation probes must retain the host’s fixed targets/candidates, remain supplementary, and consume the shared budget. Interpret findings as hypotheses; compare subsequent single-model repairs under matched budgets and the mandated macro validation HR@10. Repeated validation-guided choices can overfit the fixed 200-user/category sample, so limit and record comparisons.

References: [1] NextItNet; [2] Sequential-structure analysis; [3] Krichene and Rendle; [4] ECCR; [5] RecBole implementation; [6] Microsoft implementation; [7] Constrained shuffling; [8] FINEST, linked below.

idea.description: Implement a distance-resolved, support-aware DiagnosisProbe around the actual trained NextItNet, combining structural and deployment checks with paired history perturbations to distinguish implementation failures from temporal-dependence hypotheses.
idea.motivation: The supplied qualitative diagnosis reports broad relevance and excessive persistence of older interests, but current training-margin probes cannot establish those behaviors. The adapter offers inexpensive troubleshooting before architectural changes, while explicitly separating sensitivity, ranking accuracy, lexical evidence and unobserved user needs. Its original potential rating was optimistic without measured validation gains; implementation difficulty must include perturbation controls and saved-predictor verification.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and the host ModelView interfaces. Manage mode through view.model, the actual nn.Module; restore its previous mode in finally and use no_grad. Preserve view.log2feats(sequence), view.item_emb and view.predict_score(features, items). Retain existing all-position embedding/margin probes separately from new final-position probes. Select each row's largest index with sequence != 0, normally L-1; exclude all-padding rows and require nonzero positive and negative IDs at the original readout. Keep original targets fixed after every perturbation. Empty measurements return null and support zero; record eligible rows, distinct users when identifiable, valid positions, comparisons and exclusion reasons. Keep unavailable item-category breakdowns empty. Preserve the existing embedding-collapse definition but explain that its mapped value near 0.5 means mean cosine near zero and is not a calibrated collapse probability. Report raw margins as scale-dependent diagnostics, accompanied by pairwise negative-win rates and rank-based measurements where candidate sets are available.

Compute reachable offsets from the instantiated computation graph: initialize S={0}; each stride-one causal convolution maps S to {s+j*d : s in S, j=0,...,k-1}; residual joins union branch sets. Inspect actual kernel widths and dilations, including both convolutions in every block; do not assume the second dilation equals the first. Record maximum span and exact reachable offsets separately. Channel-only normalization and pointwise operations preserve offsets; temporal normalization or global pooling requires separate dependency analysis. With dropout disabled, change valid inputs after an interior position t and compare features through t. Compare full-sequence features at t with an identical prefix under matching padding/alignment and numerical tolerances. An unreachable-offset effect suggests an implementation or dependency-analysis problem; a zero response at a reachable offset may reflect inactive nonlinearities. Check finite scores and save/reload parity through the generated predictor on identical category routes, item mappings, truncation, padding, histories and candidates; use torch.testing.assert_close with recorded dtype-appropriate tolerances. This verification occurs in the host-authorized execution environment, without inspecting other trials.

For matched recent/older comparisons, use rows with at least three nonpadding events. For each row with n events, set m=min(3,floor((n-1)/2)); retain the final event, remove the m immediately preceding events for the recent condition, and the m oldest events for the older condition. This gives disjoint, equal-size removal sets and equal resulting lengths. Repack survivors with left padding. Also ablate exactly those selected events at the item-embedding output while retaining their positions and the original padding structure; do not simulate this by assigning item ID zero, which can change masking behavior. Implement embedding ablation through a temporary diagnostic hook or internal helper without changing public method signatures, and remove hooks in finally. Treat embedding ablation as an artificial missing-input intervention. Its difference from repacking measures perturbation-implementation sensitivity and does not isolate a causal distance effect. Prefix shuffling permutes only valid events preceding the final interaction, preserving the item multiset, final event, sequence length, padding and readout; record identity permutations and skip rows without a nontrivial permutation.

Use a diagnostic-local generator seeded 42, fixed batch/row bounds and five repeated prefix-shuffle draws. Reuse each perturbed history for all corresponding score comparisons. Record bounds, sampled row selection and draw seeds in diagnostic output; exact offset probes must record offsets tested and whether replacement items differ from originals. The supplied loader has no stable user IDs, so do not manufacture user-level intervals from its rows. When a separately permitted diagnostic path provides stable user IDs and the unchanged pinned validation candidates, average repeated draws within user and report paired HR@10 changes, target-rank changes and top-10 overlap. Define overlap as intersection size divided by 10, use the evaluator's tie handling, and bootstrap users within each category before recomputing the four-category macro mean. Use 1,000 bootstrap replicates with a separate local seed 42; intervals are conditional on fitted models, fixed candidates and the chosen perturbation procedure. Without stable IDs or permitted candidate access, mark those outputs unavailable and retain loader-pair measurements. Never substitute pairwise accuracy for benchmark HR@10 or change the evaluator.

Use only permitted titles/descriptions for optional lexical coverage; do not access unavailable ratings, reviews or item categories. Retain source snippets, denominators and unknown cases, and do not infer satisfied needs or compatibility from overlap. Keep simulator feedback from twenty training users separate from validation evidence and acknowledge its five-user/category support. The adapter does not itself train a new model or prove that robustness improves accuracy. If diagnostics justify an intervention, compare it against the corrected baseline under matched training budgets, recording category scores as well as macro validation HR@10. Avoid broad validation-driven searches and repeated optional peeking; a fixed validation subset does not eliminate adaptive overfitting. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200, batches per epoch 200, supplied splits and evaluator, all four category routes, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Load exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, without independent predictor fusion or checkpoint averaging. Any later architectural change must update the embedded predictor writer consistently and adapt the probes.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        previous_mode = view.model.training
        view.model.eval()
        diagnostic_rng = local_generator(seed=42)
        try:
            with no_grad():
                record_actual_convolutions_and_reachable_offset_sets()
                collect_existing_embedding_and_all_position_margin_metrics()
                for batch in fixed_bounded_batches(train_loader):
                    _, sequence, positive, negative = batch
                    t, nonempty = largest_nonzero_index_per_row(sequence)
                    valid = nonempty & nonzero_targets_at(positive, negative, t)
                    targets = paired_items_at_original_t(positive, negative, t)
                    base = score_original_targets_at_last_nonpadding(sequence, targets)
                    record_final_pair_margins_and_negative_wins(base, valid)

                    recent_slots, older_slots, eligible = matched_disjoint_slots(
                        sequence, m=lambda n: min(3, (n - 1) // 2), keep_final=True)
                    for selected_slots in [recent_slots, older_slots]:
                        repacked = delete_selected_events_and_left_pad(sequence, selected_slots)
                        packed_scores = score_original_targets_at_last_nonpadding(repacked, targets)
                        with temporary_embedding_output_ablation(selected_slots):
                            fixed_scores = score_at_original_readout(sequence, targets, t)
                        record_paired_changes(base, packed_scores, fixed_scores,
                                              valid & eligible)

                    for draw in range(5):
                        shuffled, eligible = shuffle_valid_prefix_keep_final(
                            sequence, diagnostic_rng)
                        record_nonidentity_shuffle_support(eligible)
                        record_paired_changes(base,
                            score_original_targets_at_last_nonpadding(shuffled, targets),
                            valid=valid & eligible)

                    check_future_changes_leave_features_through_t_unchanged(sequence)
                    check_aligned_prefix_equivalence(sequence)
                    probe_recorded_reachable_and_unreachable_offsets(sequence)

                return {'metrics': summarize_with_support_nulls_and_configuration(),
                        'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions_and_limits()}
        finally:
            remove_any_remaining_diagnostic_hooks()
            view.model.train(previous_mode)

# Separate host-authorized integration check:
reload_generated_predictor_and_compare_scores_with_training_model_and_view()

# Only if fixed validation candidates and stable user IDs are legitimately available:
# aggregate repeated perturbations within each user; compute paired ranks, HR@10,
# and top-10 overlap; bootstrap users within category, then macro-average.
# Otherwise report these measurements as unavailable.

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt_with_metrics_definitions_supports_and_configuration(
        raw_diagnosis,
        require_measurement_hypothesis_separation=True,
        forbid_intent_compatibility_or_accuracy_claims_from_sensitivity_alone=True)

originality.positive: Integrates exact NextItNet reachability, perturbation controls and generated-predictor parity into a focused diagnostic protocol.
originality.negative: The underlying techniques are established; the contribution is task-specific integration rather than a new learning algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can detect concrete implementation failures and guide controlled single-model ablations without assuming unavailable user traits.
future_potential.negative: No supplied evidence establishes that these sensitivity measurements predict validation gains, and sampled-candidate findings may not transfer to full-catalog ranking.

code_difficulty.positive: Most measurements reuse existing model hooks and bounded frozen-model inference without fitting additional predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact dependency tracing, temporary embedding ablation, target alignment, user-level uncertainty and predictor parity require careful model-specific integration.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for causal-padding, receptive-field and distance-sensitivity checks.
limitations: Architecture alone does not establish current intent, complementarity or compatibility.
Receptive-field span does not establish that every offset within that span is reachable.

related_work.title: Sequential-structure analysis (2024)
contributions: Investigates sequential structure through shuffling experiments, motivating controlled order-sensitivity measurements.
limitations: A shuffle effect does not by itself distinguish preference dynamics from other temporal structure or prove that a proposed repair improves accuracy.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled metrics can produce inconsistent model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace this task's mandated selection protocol.
Its results do not justify interpreting raw sampled-negative margins as ranking improvements.

related_work.title: ECCR (2024)
contributions: Highlights the distinction between broad relevance and compatibility with an anchor item.
limitations: Compatibility cannot be inferred reliably from interaction proximity or title overlap alone.
This task may lack sufficient explicit compatibility evidence.

related_work.title: RecBole NextItNet implementation
contributions: Provides a concrete implementation illustrating causal convolution and residual-block dilation choices, including d followed by 2d.
limitations: The supplied corrected baseline may differ; dependency analysis must inspect its actual instantiated architecture.

related_work.title: Microsoft NextItNet implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for final-position NextItNet inference.
limitations: Reference code cannot establish score parity or routing correctness for the generated RecHarness predictor.

related_work.title: Constrained shuffling research (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes user-order patterns from item-availability effects, motivating caution when interpreting shuffling.
limitations: Final-item-preserving shuffling still changes adjacency and item-to-target distances and does not isolate latent intent.

related_work.title: FINEST
contributions: Studies improving rank-list stability while preserving next-item accuracy, supporting separate measurement of stability and accuracy.
limitations: Does not validate baseline perturbation sensitivity as a predictor of improvement from a NextItNet intervention.
